outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms capable of producing a few tornadoes, very large hail, and damaging gusts are expected late this afternoon into early tonight from southeastern Nebraska to northwestern Oklahoma. More isolated severe storms will be possible farther north across Iowa and southern Minnesota, as well as along the corridor from northeastern Missouri to North Carolina.

sections.title: Southeastern NE to northwestern OK this afternoon into tonight
sections.text: A surface cold front is moving southeastward across eastern SD/NE and northwestern KS early this morning, in association with a midlevel shortwave trough crossing the northern Plains. The front will continue eastward into western MN/IA and southeastern NE to central KS by this evening, though motion of the front will slow in KS this afternoon. Meanwhile, the warm sector is demarcated by a convectively-reinforced baroclinic zone from central IL to western IA and southwestern MN, with upper 60s to near 70 F dewpoints in the corridor between the boundaries from eastern KS into eastern NE. This moisture, combined with strong surface heating and steep midlevel lapse rates, will support strong buoyancy (MLCAPE in excess of 3000 J/kg) this afternoon along and immediately ahead of the cold front, which will serve as the primary focus for severe thunderstorm development this afternoon/evening. As the surface front slows across KS by this afternoon, strong surface heating and deep mixing will result in large buoyancy and steep low-midlevel lapse rates. These profiles will favor strong low-level stretching of vertical vorticity along the boundary by new updrafts, prior to the generation of wi

sections.title: Mid MS Valley and vicinity this afternoon/evening
sections.text: Convection is ongoing in a couple of clusters from western IA to central IL, in association with low-level warm advection and MCVs. This convection will help reinforce the stalled front along the same corridor, which should focus additional storm development this afternoon as the boundary layer to the south destabilizes. One or more clusters may cross the area from northeastern MO across southern IL to KY this afternoon into early tonight, with an attendant threat for damaging winds and isolated large hail.

sections.title: NC and vicinity this afternoon/evening
sections.text: A surface cold front across central VA will continue southward today and consolidate with a remnant outflow boundary now across NC. Surface heating south of the boundaries will contribute to moderate buoyancy (MLCAPE around 1500 J/kg) this afternoon across central/southern NC, when convective initiation is expected. Vertical shear will be weak, but the strongest storms could produce isolated/short-lived downbursts. ..Thompson/Broyles.. 06/11/2018

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe storms are most likely across parts of the Lower to Mid-Missouri Valley during the late afternoon and evening. Very large hail, damaging wind gusts, and a few tornadoes are possible.

sections.title: Lower/Mid-MO Valley to Ozark Plateau
sections.text: A surface cyclone is centered over southeast SD with a cold front extending southwest into the southern High Plains. This boundary should gradually progress east with the surface low tracking southeast where the front occludes and intersects a warm front near the MO/IA border. Upper 60s to lower 70s boundary-layer dew points are prevalent within the warm sector south towards central/eastern OK. This moisture combined with nearly cloud-free insolation along with rather steep mid-level lapse rates, will support a large plume of very large buoyancy with MLCAPE of 3000-4000 J/kg. Initial storm development is anticipated near the surface cyclone over the Mid-MO Valley. The strong instability will compensate for marginally favorable wind profiles with slow storm motions. This should yield a cluster mode with embedded supercells from western IA to northeast KS. Very large hail and a few tornadoes will be possible within this corridor, mainly between 21-01Z. Thereafter, thunderstorm outflow should become more pervasive and upscale growth into one or more MCSs will be largely cold pool driven given only modest low-level warm advection tonight. As such, confidence is low in how convective ev

sections.title: Southern IL to KY
sections.text: Convection is ongoing from central IL east to the Upper OH Valley in association with weak low-level warm advection and decaying MCVs. This convection will help reinforce the stalled front from southern IL across KY, which should focus additional storm development this afternoon as the boundary layer to the south destabilizes. With weak deep-layer shear and 700 mb westerlies decreasing, the potential for an organized multicell cluster producing damaging winds appears low, but isolated damaging winds are possible.

sections.title: Carolinas
sections.text: A cold front has reached parts of central NC/SC. Scattered storms will develop along this boundary this afternoon, with moderate buoyancy (MLCAPE of 1500-2000 J/kg) common ahead of it. Vertical shear is very weak, but given the expected coverage of pulse storms, will maintain low wind probabilities for short-lived downbursts. ..Grams/Gleason.. 06/11/2018

sections.title: 20Z Update
sections.text: Extended 5% tornado probabilities slightly eastward in southwestern IA along the surface warm front that is located across this region. Backed, southeasterly low-level flow in the vicinity of this front will enhance low-level hodographs, and any thunderstorms moving along or just of the front should have at least some tornadic potential. Otherwise, no substantial changes have been made to the Slight/Enhanced risk areas. Scattered to widespread thunderstorms are still expected to develop along a cold front this afternoon across eastern NE and vicinity, with an initial threat for large to very large hail and isolated tornadoes eventually transitioning to a damaging wind threat later this evening as convection probably grows upscale into a MCS across northwestern MO and eastern KS. See Mesoscale Discussion 706 for more details on the short-term threat across eastern NE/western IA and vicinity. ..Gleason.. 06/11/2018 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1129 AM CDT Mon Jun 11 2018/

outlooks.summary: The risk for thunderstorms mainly capable of producing severe wind and some hail may still increase for a period this evening across the middle to lower Missouri Valley, before diminishing later tonight. Other strong thunderstorms remain possible farther to the southwest, across the central Plains, as well as across parts of the lower Ohio Valley.

sections.title: 01Z Outlook Update
sections.text: ...Mid/lower Missouri Valley into central Plains... An upscale growing cluster of thunderstorms is now ongoing across parts of southeast Nebraska and southwest Iowa into northwest Missouri and northeast Kansas. This appears focused in the presence of low-level convergence and weak lower/mid tropospheric warm advection, near the intersection of two frontal zones across the middle to lower Missouri Valley. This is just south of the mid-latitude westerlies, but beneath strongly difluent upper flow that may be contributing to convective development. The convective system is evolving within rather modest deep layer westerly mean flow on the order of 10-20 kt, with perhaps some semblance of a south/southwesterly low-level jet (20 to perhaps 30 kt) roughly along an axis from near Wichita KS toward the St. Joseph MO area. This may promote a continuing general southeastward and southward propagation of convection into Missouri and eastern Kansas this evening. Given the larger-scale environment, forward propagation may be at a rather modest speed, but it is at least possible that rear inflow jet/surface cold pool strengthening could support an acceleration that could be accompanied by increa

sections.title: Lower Ohio Valley
sections.text: Forcing associated with a weak convectively generated perturbation may be contributing to an ongoing increase in thunderstorm development across southern Illinois. Although deep layer flow/shear is generally weak southeastward through the lower Ohio Valley, some further increase in intensification may still be possible in the presence of moderately large CAPE. The evolution of a small but vigorous cold pool accompanied by a risk for strong surface gusts approaching severe limits may not be out of the question before activity diminishes in waning instability later tonight. ..Kerr.. 06/12/2018

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe thunderstorms capable of all severe hazards, including tornadoes, are expected to begin developing within the next 2 hours. A Tornado Watch will likely be needed.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Cumulus field continues to increases within the narrow warm sector across eastern NE, just ahead of an approaching cold front. Recent surface analysis places a low about 30 mi north of YKN in far southeast SD, with a cold front extending southwestward across eastern NE and into central KS. A warm front also extends southeastward from the low across far southwest IA and north-central/northwest MO. High-resolution visible satellite imagery also appears to reveal a southwestward progressing outflow boundary beneath the thicker clouds over far southeast SD. Warm-sector between these features is characterized by temperatures in the upper 80s, dewpoints in upper 60s/low 70s, and strong instability. Latest mesoanalysis estimates MLCAPE over 3000 J/kg with little, if any, convective inhibition remaining immediately ahead of the front. Consequently, continued convergence in this environment will likely lead to convective initiation within the next hour or so. Once this occurs, rapid thunderstorm development is anticipated with storms quickly becoming severe. Primary severe threat appears to be large hail, some of which could be greater than 2 inches in diameter. Additionally, the favorable low-level shear may contribute to some increased tornado potential as well. Tall, water-loaded updrafts will also result in a threat for strong wind gusts. A watch will likely be needed across portions of the area to address this anticipated severe threat.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe thunderstorms may develop across north-central and central KS this afternoon. Trends are being monitored for possible watch issuance.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent visible satellite imagery shows an increasing agitated cu field along and just ahead of the approaching cold front. Airmass south of the front is well-mixed with temperatures in the upper 90s/low 100s and dewpoints in the mid 60s. This mixing has eroded much the convective inhibition and the expectation is for continued convergence along the cold front to result in eventual convective initiation. However, given the amount of dry mid-level air (sampled well by the 19Z TOP sounding), there is some question as to how long it will be before this initiation takes place. Additionally, convergence decreases with southern extent across KS, casting uncertainty regarding the occurrence of thunderstorms into central KS in the near-term. As a result, a conditional risk for severe hail and wind exists across north-central/central KS. Trends will be monitored for convective development and possible watch issuance.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Locally, strong damaging wind gusts are possible through the late afternoon to early evening across southeast Kentucky into northeast Tennessee and perhaps far southwest Virginia. WW issuance is unlikely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Trends in mosaic radar imagery showed a short band of storms in central KY, extending from Mercer to Marion Counties, and moving to the east-southeast at 25-30 kt. Additional isolated storms had developed along an old outflow boundary which was analyzed from northeast TN through south-central KY to southern IL. The ongoing band of storms in central KY had the strongest forward motion which should persist as they track along an instability gradient into southeast KY, northeast TN, and perhaps affecting part of far southwest VA. This motion and potential severe wind threat could be enhanced some, given stronger winds of 35-40 kt observed on the LVX VWP in the 3-5 km layer. Spatiotemporal limitations will preclude the issuance of a severe thunderstorm watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated severe storms possible along a warm frontal boundary. No WW issuance is anticipated at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Isolated strong to potentially severe storms have initiated along a warm front from northeast of IRK to east of EVV. Modest low-level shear (0-3km SRH of up to 150 m2/s2) coinciding with 2500+ J/kg MLCAPE along the warm front suggest that the more intense updrafts may briefly acquire low-level rotation. As such, isolated marginal instances of severe gusty winds and large hail are possible and a very brief tornado cannot be out ruled. Given the very isolated and marginal extent of the severe threat, a WW issuance is not currently anticipated.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated storms capable of hail and wind are possible across western Oklahoma this evening, but a watch is unlikely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Visible imagery shows a substantial CU field across western OK where hot temperatures have removed CIN along the dryline. Meanwhile, robust low-level moisture remains in place with southeasterly surface winds. The result is very strong instability, and a zone of uncapped air. Surface convergence near the dryline may be sufficient for a few storms this evening, with weakly veering winds with height supporting a south or southwestward motion. Hail and locally damaging wind will be possible should storms initiate.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A threat of damaging wind and hail continues across the watch area, and may extend into the remainder of southeast Kansas and western Missouri this evening.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An MCS stretches from northeast KS into south central IA as of 0230Z. Northern portions of the line previously contained measured severe winds, but, may begin to weaken a bit as the most unstable air remains to the southwest. The bulk of the MCS was beginning to propagate in a more southerly direction, with locally damaging outflow winds along with embedded hail cores. A very unstable air mass extends from OK across eastern KS, and this air mass should maintain the MCS as it travels across the severe thunderstorm watch. Another watch may be needed later this evening for portions of southeast KS and western MO, should the storms still be severe at that time. Farther north into central IA, the threat appears more marginal for both wind and hail, with a gradual weakening trend expected as these storms encounter a stabilizing air mass due to cool east winds. ..Jewell.. 06/12/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe threat ongoing in eastern Kansas will likely continue for several more hours. Large hail and wind damage can be expected with the stronger thunderstorms associated with the MCS. Additional watch issuance may be needed across southeast Kansas as the expiration of WW 173 takes place at 1 am CDT. The threat is expected to become marginal across northern Oklahoma where a weather watch probably will not be needed.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A linear MCS is currently moving southeastward into a strongly unstable airmass across eastern Kansas and western Missouri where the RAP is showing MLCAPE values in the 3000 to 4000 J/kg range. This will likely fuel the MCS for several more hours as it moves southeastward into the stronger instability. Although deep-layer shear on regional WSR-88D VWPs is only around 30 kt, 850 mb flow will be maintained or gradually strengthen across southeast Kansas over the next few hours. This along with the instability and shear will likely maintain a severe threat with the stronger thunderstorms. Large hail will be most likely with lingering supercells. Wind damage will also be possible along the leading edge of the MCS. The severe threat is expected to become marginal as the storms reach northern Oklahoma and southwest Missouri later tonight.
